minutes.summary: The committee reviewed Town Meeting, where voters funded a study of what the same program would cost in a new building, and discussed how to scope the summer architect work. Members debated whether the new-build comparison is truly apples to apples and whether to hold community visioning sessions. Three sets of prior minutes were approved and the next meeting was set for June 16th.

what_happened.line: The committee took no budget vote; it met to debrief after Town Meeting funded a study of what the same program would cost in a new building.
The study funding also sits in the fiscal 2022 town budget, which starts July 1st.
Members debated whether the new-build comparison with renovating the seven-year-old building is truly apples to apples; the discussion ended without a resolution.
The chair will talk with the architect's new project manager and put planning of the study scope on a June agenda.
The next meeting was set for June 16th at 5:30, with a community visioning session to go on that agenda.

why_it_matters: Voters may later be asked to choose between renovating the existing building and building new, and how the study defines a comparable program will shape what that choice looks like.
The study is paid for through the town budget, mostly taxes, so its scope decides what information residents will have before any larger borrowing vote.
